cross_pr_comparison.git_history_note: Commit 9b59a19f8 / 79de4f195 ('test(customizer): settle the remounted preview before selecting paper size', authored 2026-09-15T01:48:23-06:00 by the same repo owner) is an ANCESTOR of the ee87fe5/9be00ebe commit and already added `expectSheetType`+paper-size settle assertions at TWO other tab-switch points in this exact test (after switching back to the Atlas tab, and after switching to the Locust tab later in the test -- spec.ts diff hunks at old lines 366-375 and 382-391). It did NOT add an equivalent settle wait for the THIRD tab-switch point -- the `loadLocustBesideAtlas(page)` call at spec.ts:354, which happens while Atlas's print is deliberately stalled. That is exactly the gap this flake lives in: the author already diagnosed and partially fixed 'a remounted preview needs to settle before the next assertion' as a real bug pattern in this file, earlier the same day, but the fix did not cover the specific concurrent-print-plus-unit-load window.

code_reading.content_summary: Test body. Loads Atlas, prints once ('letterPrint'). Registers `page.route('**/record-sheets/biped_pips/**', ..., { times: 1 })` (line 339-347) that intercepts ONLY the first matching network request, calls `sawPips()`, then `await heldPips` (holds the request open) before `route.continue()`. Clicks Print (line 349). Inside a try/finally (350-357): awaits the stalled route firing (`requestedPips`), asserts the popup isn't closed and printCount is still 0, then calls `await loadLocustBesideAtlas(page)` (line 354) WHILE the print's network request is still held open. The `finally` block (356) unconditionally calls `releasePips()`. Line 358 then polls `printCount(page)` to become 1 within the global 10s expect timeout.

`installPrintHarness` monkey-patches `window.open` so the popup's `.print()` synchronously snapshots `doc.querySelectorAll('body > svg')` -- i.e. whatever HTML the product already wrote into the popup by the time `.print()` is called. `printCount`/`printCaptures` just read `window.__printHarness.prints.length` / contents. `printOnce` (used by other tests, not this one) polls `printCount` the same way.

`printRecordSheet(data, paperSize)`: opens the popup SYNCHRONOUSLY before any await (comment explicitly calls this out, to survive popup blockers), then `await this.getSVGString(data, paperSize)` (the async, potentially slow step), then writes the built HTML into the ALREADY-CAPTURED `printWindow` reference and calls `printWindow.print()`. `data` was extracted as a plain, fully value-copied object by `extractData`/`extractArmor` BEFORE this call (see dataExtractors.armor.ts below) -- it is not a live reference into any store, so a concurrent unit switch cannot corrupt its *content*. This rules out a store-mutation/content-leak explanation for the printCount:0 case; the bug is about completion TIMING, not about which unit's data gets used.

`extractArmor` builds a brand-new plain object literal per call from primitive numbers on `unit.armor.allocation.*`. No shared/mutable references are carried into the extracted `IRecordSheetArmor`. Confirms print data is a true snapshot.

`fillArmorPips` -> `loadAllArmorPips`: `armor.locations.map(async (loc) => { ... await loadAndInsertPips(...) ... })` then `await Promise.all(pipPromises)` (line ~106-108, `loadAllArmorPips`). This is PARALLEL, not sequential -- roughly 8-10 concurrent `fetch()` calls per unit (one per armor location, front + rear). The test's `page.route(..., { times: 1 })` intercepts only the FIRST of these, so `Promise.all` for the Atlas print is blocked on exactly one stalled promise while its siblings resolve normally; the whole `fillArmorPips`/`getSVGString`/`printRecordSheet` chain is gated on that one promise.

`loadSVG` (used for the SVG *template*, not the per-location pip files, which fetch raw via armor.ts directly) has a string-content cache keyed by path and a single-flight `configLoadPromise` guard for config JSON only. No shared/cross-call locking that could serialize Locust's asset loads behind Atlas's stalled one -- ruled out as the mechanism.

Each `RecordSheetService.getMechSVGString` call constructs a brand-new `SVGRecordSheetRenderer` -> new `TemplateRecordSheetRenderer` -> a fresh `DOMParser().parseFromString(...)` per call (verified in template.ts:35-38 `parseSVGTemplate`, no shared/cached DOM node keyed by template path). `mount()` appends an off-screen container directly to the real `document.body` (line ~134-141) -- a genuinely shared global DOM resource, but each call gets its OWN container, so two concurrent renders (Atlas's print + Locust's fresh preview) do not touch the same nodes. Ruled out as a direct data-race; the real cost is that BOTH renders are doing substantial SYNCHRONOUS main-thread work (DOMParser parse, per-location pip DOM construction/cloning, XMLSerializer.serializeToString) that cannot overlap on Chromium's single JS thread -- they compete for wall-clock time, not correctness.

`onPrint` is a `React.useCallback` closed over `[unitObject, paperSize]` bound to the Print button's onClick; since it is invoked synchronously at click time (Atlas was active), the promise chain it kicks off is a plain, non-reactive async function -- switching tabs afterward does not cancel or redirect it (no AbortController anywhere in this path; grep confirmed none exist under src/components/customizer/ or src/services/printing/). The ON-SCREEN preview is a SEPARATE pipeline (`useRecordSheetCanvasRenderer`, lines 116-153) with its own `generationRef` staleness guard per mounted instance, keyed off `[unitObject, paperSize]` -- this explains PR1705's failure mode: Locust's own preview render is a fresh, independent async chain that has to run to completion and commit before `expectSheetType(page,'Locust LCT-1V')` can observe it; under load it simply had not finished within 10s, so the poll kept observing the last-committed ('Atlas AS7-D') capture.
`workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined` (single-worker on CI), `timeout: 30_000` (per-test), `expect: { timeout: 10_000 }` (the fixed poll timeout every one of the three failures hit).

'Customizer Regressions' job: `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` (GitHub-hosted, 2 vCPU / 7GB standard runner), builds production app first (`npm run build` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE=true`), then runs `node scripts/playwright/run-playwright.mjs test e2e/customizer-equipment-catalog.spec.ts e2e/customizer-record-sheet-rendering.spec.ts e2e/customizer-edit-recovery.spec.ts --project=chromium --retries=0 --trace=retain-on-failure`. No `--workers` override here (defers to playwright.config.ts's CI default of 1). `--retries=0` means any flake fails the job outright with no automatic retry -- matches the observed 'always fails outright, passes on manual rerun' pattern.

hypothesis.summary: Not a logic/correctness bug. The test deliberately creates two concurrent, CPU-bound record-sheet render pipelines -- (1) Atlas's print, held open mid-flight via a stalled network route, and (2) a fresh full preview render for a newly-loaded Locust unit, triggered while (1) is still stalled -- and then requires BOTH to finish and settle inside a single fixed 10-second `expect.poll` window once the stall is released. Both pipelines do substantial synchronous main-thread work per unit (DOMParser parse of a template SVG with hundreds of nodes, ~8-10 parallel armor/structure pip fetches each followed by synchronous DOM cloning, XMLSerializer serialization) that cannot overlap on Chromium's single JS thread. On GitHub's standard 2 vCPU 'ubuntu-latest' runner, with `workers: 1` (so this is the only thing running in that job, but Chromium itself, the Node test-runner process, and the Node app server all still contend for those 2 cores), the combined tail latency of finishing both pipelines occasionally exceeds the fixed 10s margin. Both observed failure shapes are consistent with this single mechanism: sometimes the PRINT side is what's still catching up when the poll gives up (printCount stuck at 0 -- PR1722, PR1730); sometimes the PREVIEW side is what's still catching up (stale 'Atlas AS7-D' capture instead of 'Locust LCT-1V' -- PR1705, an earlier revision of the same test before two (but not all three) settle-assertions were added in commit 9b59a19f8/79de4f195 earlier the same day). Everything eventually completes correctly given enough wall-clock time -- attempt 2 of the identical commit passed for both PR1722 and PR1730 with zero code changes.

why_not_alternatives.shared_fixture_or_store_leak: Ruled out: extractData/extractArmor produce fully value-copied plain objects per call (dataExtractors.armor.ts:14-155); the print's `data` argument cannot be mutated by a later unit load.
why_not_alternatives.stale_zustand_store: No direct evidence found of a shared mutable store field read by the print pipeline after the click; RecordSheetService.printRecordSheet operates only on the already-captured `data`/`printWindow` local variables, not on live component/store state.
why_not_alternatives.shared_DOM_template_cache: Ruled out: parseSVGTemplate does a fresh DOMParser().parseFromString() per call (template.ts:35-38); TemplateRecordSheetRenderer.mount() appends its own off-screen container per instance, not a shared one.
why_not_alternatives.abort_controller_cancellation: Ruled out: grep found no AbortController usage anywhere under src/components/customizer/ or src/services/printing/.

local_reproduction.why: ALL 30 test-runs in the file failed (not just the target test), every one at the very first `waitForBacking`/`expectSheetType` assertion for Atlas -- before Locust is ever loaded, before the print button is ever clicked, before the deliberate network stall is ever installed. The failure screenshot (test-results/customizer-record-sheet-re-29763-e-selected-paper-customizer-chromium/test-failed-1.png) shows the on-screen preview canvas displaying the product's own caught-error placeholder text 'Error rendering record sheet' (src/components/customizer/preview/RecordSheetCanvasPreview.tsx:62-78 `drawRecordSheetRenderError`, which sets canvas.width/height to the plain PAPER_DIMENSIONS[paperSize] = 612x792 -- exactly the 'received' value in every failure). This is the catch-path in `renderUnitRecordSheetPreview` (RecordSheetCanvasPreview.tsx:53-59), meaning `RecordSheetService.getSVGString` threw for every single render attempt. Root cause of THIS local failure: `public/record-sheets/` in this worktree contains only `mm-data-version.json` -- the actual template/pip SVG assets were never fetched (`npm run fetch:assets` was not run for this worktree), so the local-path fetch source 404s; the fallback CDN sources (jsdelivr, raw.githubusercontent.com) were reachable with 200 OK from this orchestrator's own shell (verified via curl), but the record-sheet render clearly still failed inside the Playwright-launched Chromium instance for every run, consistent with that specific browser process lacking the same network path (a sandboxing/proxy difference between the host shell and the spawned browser, not investigated further as it is out of scope for a read-only diagnosis and does not bear on the CI race).
local_reproduction.conclusion: This local environment gap (missing fetched assets / browser-side asset fetch failure) is unrelated to, and fully explains away, the 5/5 local failures -- it is NOT evidence about the intermittent CI race, and must not be read as such. Per the task's own guidance, reasoning about the actual race falls back to the CI log evidence above (three independent CI failures, two of them byte-identical reruns-pass-clean on the same commit, all hitting a fixed 10s wall-clock predicate at the same test position, immediately after code that deliberately creates two concurrent CPU-bound render pipelines) rather than a guess.

fix_candidates_ranked.title: Sequence the two concurrent render pipelines inside the test itself: wait for Locust's own preview to fully settle before releasing the held print request
fix_candidates_ranked.file_line: e2e/customizer-record-sheet-rendering.spec.ts:354 (immediately after `await loadLocustBesideAtlas(page);`, still inside the `try` block, before the `finally` at line 355 runs `releasePips()`)
fix_candidates_ranked.change: Insert `await waitForBacking(page, LETTER);` and `await expectSheetType(page, 'Locust LCT-1V');` right after line 354, before the try block ends. This drains Locust's CPU-bound preview render to completion BEFORE the stalled Atlas print is released, so the two heavy synchronous render pipelines no longer have to race each other inside the same 10s window -- the print's post-release completion then only has to compete with an already-idle main thread, matching the pattern the same author already applied at two other tab-switch points in this exact file earlier the same day (commit 9b59a19f8/79de4f195).
fix_candidates_ranked.red_first_pin: Before this fix, run the test in isolation with an artificial CPU throttle (e.g. Chromium CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` at 4-6x, settable via a temporary `page.context().newCDPSession(page)` call, or simply run with `--repeat-each=10` under a deliberately loaded machine) to show the printCount:0 / stale-type failure reproduces locally when the two pipelines are forced to overlap under load; after adding the settle-wait, the same throttled run should pass because the two heavy render passes no longer overlap.
fix_candidates_ranked.why_not_a_timeout_widen: Does not touch playwright.config.ts's `expect.timeout` or add any `test.slow()`/per-assertion timeout override. It removes the CPU contention between the two pipelines by sequencing them, which is what the fixed 10s margin was implicitly assuming in the first place.

fix_candidates_ranked.title: Same fix, defense in depth: also settle Atlas's on-screen preview state before asserting `letterPrint.typeName` at line 360
